n: Leaving the temple for the last time, Jesus’s disciples point out its impressive buildings. Herod the Great had expanded it into one of the ancient world’s grandest structures.

f.g: Some of Herod’s foundation stones weighed many tons; the work continued for decades.

n: Jesus shocks them: not one stone will be left standing on another. Roman armies fulfilled this in AD 70.

f.w: There shall not be left here one stone upon another

n: On the Mount of Olives, facing the temple, the disciples ask two questions: when will the temple fall, and what will signal his coming and the end of the world? This begins the Olivet Discourse.

f.g: The Joseph Smith Translation adds “or the destruction of the wicked.”

n: Jesus’s first concern is that they not be deceived.

f.w: Take heed that no man deceive you

n: Many will come claiming to be the Messiah and will mislead many people.
Wars and rumors of wars will come, but don’t panic — these alone don’t mean the end has arrived.
Nations will fight one another, and there will be famines, epidemics, and earthquakes in many places.

f.g: Plagues, epidemics.
divers = various.

n: These are only the beginning — like the first pains of childbirth before the new age is born.

f.g: Greek ōdin — birth pains.

n: Disciples will be persecuted, handed over, and killed, hated everywhere for bearing Christ’s name.

f.w: deliver you up to be afflicted

n: Many will fall away and turn on one another.

f.g: Stumble and fall away from faith.

n: False prophets will arise and lead many astray.
As wickedness increases, many people’s love will grow cold.

f.g: wax = grow, become.

n: Those who stay faithful to the end will be saved.

f.w: he that shall endure unto the end

n: Before the end, the gospel will be preached to all nations as a witness. Latter-day Saints see worldwide missionary work as part of this fulfillment.

f.w: this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world

n: Daniel’s “abomination of desolation” — a desecration of the holy place — signals disaster. Fulfilled when Rome defiled and destroyed the temple, it has a latter-day fulfillment too.

f.g: Something detestable that brings ruin, especially desecration of the sanctuary.

n: When that happens, those in Judea should flee to the mountains immediately. Early Christians reportedly fled to Pella before Jerusalem fell.
There will be no time to gather possessions. Someone on a flat rooftop should take the outside stairs and run.

f.g: Flat roofs were used as living space and often reached by outside stairs.

n: A worker in the field shouldn’t even go back for his cloak.

f.g: His outer cloak, often left at the field’s edge while working.

n: Jesus expresses compassion for pregnant women and nursing mothers, for whom fleeing would be especially hard.

f.g: Nursing mothers.

n: Pray that you won’t have to flee in winter, when roads flood, or on the Sabbath, when travel was limited and gates were shut.
The distress will be unmatched. Josephus describes horrific suffering during the Roman siege of Jerusalem.
If those days weren’t cut short, no one would survive; for the sake of God’s chosen, they will be shortened.

f.g: God’s chosen people — in JS—Matthew, “the elect according to the covenant.”

n: Don’t believe anyone who says the Messiah is here or there.
False Christs and prophets will perform impressive signs, almost able to deceive even God’s chosen.

f.w: if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect

n: Jesus has warned them in advance so they won’t be caught off guard.
Don’t go chasing rumors of a hidden Messiah in the desert or in secret rooms.

f.g: Inner rooms — a secret hiding place.

n: His real coming will be unmistakable — as visible as lightning flashing across the whole sky.

f.w: as the lightning cometh out of the east

n: Where a carcass lies, birds of prey gather — a proverb about inevitability. Joseph Smith’s translation applies it to the gathering of the elect from all the earth.

f.g: Probably vultures (the Greek word covers both).
carcase = carcass, dead body.

n: After the tribulation, the heavens themselves will be shaken — dramatic signs in sun, moon, and stars.

f.r: Isaiah 13:10; Joel 2:10, 31; D&C 45:42; D&C 88:87; Joseph Smith—Matthew 1:33

n: The sign of the Son of Man will appear, the nations will mourn, and all will see him coming on the clouds in power and glory.

f.w: coming in the clouds of heaven
all the tribes of the earth mourn

n: He will send angels with a great trumpet blast to gather his chosen from every direction.

f.w: a great sound of a trumpet

f.g: All four directions — the whole earth.

n: Learn from the fig tree: when its branches get tender and sprout leaves, you know summer is near.

f.w: a parable of the fig tree

n: In the same way, when these signs appear, his coming is close — right at the door.
“This generation” will see these things fulfilled. JS—Matthew clarifies it means the generation in which the signs are shown.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but Jesus’s words are absolutely certain.

f.w: my words shall not pass away

n: No one knows the exact day or hour — not even the angels. Only the Father knows. Date-setting is pointless; readiness is everything.

f.w: of that day and hour knoweth no man

n: His coming will be like the days of Noah.

f.g: Noe = Noah.

n: Before the Flood people went on with ordinary life — eating, drinking, marrying — right up until Noah entered the ark. The problem wasn’t daily life; it was ignoring God’s warning.
They didn’t realize what was happening until the flood swept them away. So it will be when the Son of Man comes.

f.w: knew not until the flood came

n: Two people will be working side by side in a field; one will be taken and the other left — a sudden separation.

f.w: the one shall be taken, and the other left

n: Two women grinding grain together at a hand mill — one taken, one left.

f.g: Women ground daily flour with a small stone hand mill, often in pairs.

n: So stay alert and ready, since you don’t know the hour of your Lord’s coming.

f.g: Stay awake, be alert.

n: If a homeowner knew when a thief would come, he would stay awake and keep his house from being broken into.

f.g: Here a period of the night, as in 14:25.
broken into — houses of mud brick could be dug through.

n: Be ready at all times; Christ will come when people least expect him.
A parable: who is the faithful, wise servant put in charge of his master’s household to give everyone food at the right time?

f.g: meat = food; in due season = at the proper time.

n: Blessed is the servant whom the master finds faithfully doing his job when he returns.
The faithful servant will be put in charge of all the master’s possessions.
But a wicked servant tells himself the master won’t be back for a long time.
So he abuses his fellow servants and joins the drunkards.

f.g: smite = strike, beat.

n: His master will show up on a day and hour he doesn’t expect.

f.w: when he looketh not for him

n: He will be severely punished and placed with the hypocrites, where there is weeping and bitter regret.

f.g: An image of harsh punishment — literally “cut in two.”
